diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is always possible to decompose $f(p)$ into a contribution in $V$ and one in its orthogonal complement, i.e. $f(p) = f_V(p) + f_{V^\perp}(p)$.
It is an example of a manifold for which a non-linear encoder is necessary.

issues.failure_explanation: Every parameterization f admits the orthogonal decomposition f = f_V + f_{V^\perp} (as the paper itself notes in Proposition sec:lem_enc), so the class 'manifolds described by f = f_V + f_{V^\perp}' is the class of all manifolds. The actual requirement from sec:lem_enc is that f_V be injective (invertible) so that the linear projection onto V is injective on M; this hypothesis is dropped from the statement. As written the proposition is contradicted by the paper's own noisy-coil example, which requires a nonlinear encoder.

failure_location.quote: (A linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ manifolds described by $f = f_V + f_{V^\perp}$)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that f_V (the component of f in the subspace V onto which the linear encoder projects) is injective, i.e. the manifold is a graph over a linear subspace.
issues.overall_effect: The characterization of manifolds representable by a linear encoder / nonlinear decoder, and the summary claim in the main results, are not correctly stated; the design guidance 'justifies the use of a linear encoder' lacks its actual condition.
issues.title: Linear–nonlinear autoencoder proposition omits the injectivity hypothesis on f_V, making the statement vacuous/false
issues.why_classification: A local insertion of the missing hypothesis, already present in the supporting Proposition sec:lem_enc, fixes the statement without losing content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A sufficient condition for the width to ensure injectivity of the encoder is $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$, for $\ell = 1,\ldots, L-1$.
By \Cref{th:uap}, we have that $n_\ell = n_\text{in}+n_\text{out}$ is sufficient to satisfy $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ and $\lim_{|\myw|\to\infty}\Varepsilon_2 = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: A layer y = σ(Wy'+b) with n_ℓ ≥ n_{ℓ-1} is not injective in general: W may be rank-deficient and the activations used (ReLU/PReLU, and non-injective σ generally) destroy injectivity regardless of width, so the stated width condition is not sufficient. Conversely, injectivity of the encoder on M does not require each layer to be injective on all of R^{n_{ℓ-1}} (indeed the final layer maps to n < n_in and cannot be). The appeal to th:uap only yields approximation of a continuous map by some network of width n_in+n_out, not that a network of that width is injective or reproduces the identity exactly (ε_1 = 0). The theorem's 'sufficient condition' is therefore unproven and, read literally, false.

failure_location.quote: To ensure the injectivity of the encoder approximated by a neural network, each layer must be injective, condition which is satisfied when $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$ for all hidden layers

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem as an existence result: for widths n_ℓ ≥ n_in (+n_out) there exist weights such that the encoder approximates an injective embedding of M arbitrarily well (via th:uap), and separately argue (or assume) that intermediate reductions below the embedding dimension of M preclude injectivity; drop the claim that the width condition itself guarantees injectivity.
issues.overall_effect: The central architectural guideline (no intermediate reduction; reduce only at the last layer) and its use in th:fully_works ('by th:uap and th:reduction the error κ can be made arbitrarily small') rest on an invalid argument; the statement must be reinterpreted as an existence/expressivity result rather than a sufficient condition on widths.
issues.title: Theorem th:reduction: layer width n_ℓ ≥ n_{ℓ-1} does not ensure injectivity of a layer or of the encoder
issues.why_classification: The conclusion changes from a sufficient condition to an existence/expressivity statement and needs a contained replacement argument, but the design message and downstream use survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $B_r((t,\mu))\to U$ has a continuous inverse, thus $B_r((t,\mu))\to U$ is a local homeomorphism. We conclude that $U$ is locally Euclidean
Global injectivity can be obtained by augmenting the solution set with parameters and time

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis is only local injectivity on small balls. The image of a locally injective continuous map need not be a manifold: e.g. N=3, u_{N0}(μ)=(0,sin μ,sin 2μ) on P=[0,2π], F_N=(1,0,0), so u_N(t;μ)=(t,sin μ,sin 2μ) is locally injective, continuous, well-posed, but the image is a figure-eight times an interval, which is not locally Euclidean at the self-intersection. The proof only shows that U=u_N(B_r) is homeomorphic to a closed ball; it does not show U is open in the whole solution set (in the subspace topology other branches enter every neighborhood), so 'locally Euclidean' does not follow. Additionally, [0,T]×P has boundary (t=0, t=T, ∂P), so even under global injectivity the set is a manifold with boundary, not an a-manifold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to global injectivity of (t,μ)↦u_N on [0,T]×P (or use the augmented set of remark:augmentation) and weaken the conclusion to 'compact a-manifold with boundary' homeomorphic to [0,T]×P; adjust th:latent_dim to invoke Menger–Nöbeling for compact metric spaces of dimension a.
issues.overall_effect: The manifold structure of the solution set, as summarized in the main results and conclusions, is not established under the stated hypotheses; th:latent_dim, whose proof takes the topological dimension a from th:manifold, inherits the gap (though it can be salvaged via finite fibers and Menger–Nöbeling for compact spaces).
issues.title: Theorem th:manifold: local injectivity of (t,μ)↦u_N does not make the solution set an a-manifold
issues.why_classification: The repair replaces a hypothesis by a materially stronger one (local → global injectivity) and weakens the conclusion, but a recognizably comparable result survives and the paper already contemplates the augmentation route.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We now assume the construction of an autoencoder that realizes an orthogonal projection. This property can be achieved, for example, constructing the decoder as $J_\Psi = (J_{\Psi'}^\top J_{\Psi'})^{-1}J_{\Psi'}^\top$
so the bound on the timestep of the \node\ is, in the worst scenario, the same as that of the \Node.

issues.failure_explanation: For an orthogonal projection P and a general matrix Λ, the nonzero eigenvalues of PΛ are not a subset of the eigenvalues of Λ: with Λ=diag(-1,-2) and P the orthogonal projection onto span{(1,1)}, PΛ has eigenvalues 0 and -3/2. The stated conclusion requires the additional (unstated) hypothesis that col(J_Ψ) is Λ-invariant; orthogonality of the projection alone is neither sufficient nor the relevant property. The invariance does hold when the linear autoencoder exactly reproduces the (Λ-invariant) linear solution manifold, but this argument is not given.

failure_location.quote: Due to the specific assumptions made in the construction of the decoder, the projection sets some eigenvalues to zero while leaving the others unchanged. Therefore, the eigenvalues $\neq 0$ are those of $\Lambda$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that col(J_Ψ) is invariant under Λ (which follows from exact reproduction of the linear solution manifold), and derive the eigenvalue statement from invariance rather than from orthogonality.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the reduced FE stability bound is at worst that of the N-ODE for orthogonal-projection autoencoders is unsupported as stated; the proposed penalty term does not by itself deliver the promised timestep guarantee.
issues.title: Unjustified claim that the orthogonal projection leaves the nonzero eigenvalues of Λ unchanged
issues.why_classification: A short local argument with an added standard hypothesis (invariant subspace) restores the stated conclusion in the intended setting.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A necessary condition to meet the requirement $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\tau_n^k, \zeta_k \to 0$ and $\kappa \to 0$.
It follows that a necessary condition for $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\|J_{N_{\Psi'}}(t_k)-J_{\Psi'}(t_k)\|_\infty \to 0$
Reducing $\Delta t$ further leads to an increase in the error.

issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting eq:diff_op_tau from the zero-residual identity gives Σ_p β_p (N_{F_n}-F_n)(t_{j+1-p}) = τ_n^j + (1/Δt_train) Σ_p α_p [Ψ'(u_N+ζ)-Ψ'(u_N)+κ](t_{j+1-p}). The encoder-error and data-error terms are divided by Δt_train; since Σα_p = 0 they behave like time derivatives, i.e. like ∇κ·F_N and (ζ_{j+1}-ζ_j)/Δt_train, so sup-norm smallness of κ and ζ (κ → 0, ζ → 0) does not make them vanish—C¹-closeness of the encoder (as the paper itself notes for the semi data-driven case) is needed, and the joint limit Δt_train → 0 with fixed κ diverges. Moreover for P ≥ 2 only the β-weighted combination is controlled, which does not force each N_{F_n}(t_k)-F_n(t_k) to zero. The stated conclusion 'convergent method ... max‖N_{F_n}-F_n‖ → 0' is therefore not derived, and the listed conditions are neither shown sufficient nor correctly identified.

failure_location.quote: Then, setting \eqref{eq:what_nn_learns_1} to zero and comparing it to \eqref{eq:diff_op_tau}, we conclude that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume/prove C¹ (Jacobian) approximation of the encoder and that (ζ_{j+1}-ζ_j)/Δt_train → 0 (e.g. via local truncation of M_N), then carry out the subtraction with Σα_p=0 explicitly, restricting to one-step schemes or adding an argument that the β-combination controls pointwise differences; restate th:fully_works with these hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The claim ε_{F_n}(Δt_train,w) → 0 as |w| → ∞, Δt_train → 0, and hence the limit statement of th:global_convergence (which invokes th:fully_works), is unsupported for the fully data-driven strategy; the paper's own experiments show error growth when Δt < Δt_train.
issues.title: Proposition th:fully_works: zero residual loss does not imply N_{F_n} → F_n under κ, ζ → 0 (errors are divided by Δt_train)
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial replacement argument with strengthened (C¹) hypotheses is needed; the convergence claim can plausibly be recovered but not by the argument given.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $C_{1,\mu} > 0$ generally depends of the specific r.h.s. at hand and time integration scheme.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses Lipschitz constants L_Ψ and L_{F_n} (Gronwall) and an O(Δt^P) global error for the ODE ẇ = N_{F_n}(w), which requires N_{F_n} to be Lipschitz and C^P-smooth; mere continuity of Ψ', Ψ, F_n (and nothing at all assumed on N_{F_n}, which uses PReLU in the experiments) does not deliver these. The constant C_{1,μ} depends on derivatives of N_{F_n}, hence on w, so the bound's uniformity in |w| is not established either.

failure_location.quote: We make the following assumptions: $\Psi'$, $\Psi$, and $F_n$ are continuous functions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses of th:L_{F_n} (Lipschitz Ψ, Ψ', Jacobian bounds) and C^P regularity/Lipschitz continuity of N_{F_n} uniformly in the network family, and state that C_1 may depend on N_{F_n}.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's hypotheses do not support the stated bound; as written the estimate is unproven, though it holds under standard additional regularity assumptions.
issues.title: th:global_convergence assumes only continuity but uses Lipschitz constants and an order-P time-discretization bound
issues.why_classification: Standard regularity hypotheses, already used elsewhere in the paper, close the gap without changing the conclusion or rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We observe a consistent overestimation of the total concentration.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposed term sums the squared componentwise reconstruction errors, which is exactly the squared 2-norm reconstruction loss N^1_{ij} (up to the identification of the target). It contains no information about the total Σ_k [u]_k versus Σ_k [N_Ψ]_k, so its minimization cannot enforce Σ_k [u_N(t)]_k = Σ_k [u_{N0}]_k beyond what the ordinary reconstruction loss already does. The reported systematic drift of the total concentration is consistent with no conservation constraint being imposed.

failure_location.quote: a simple strategy is to modify the loss function by adding a contribution whose minimization enforces conservation

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term by a penalty on the total, e.g. (Σ_k [u_{N,i}^j]_k − Σ_k [N_Ψ(ũ_{n,i}^j)]_k)^2 (or on Σ_k [N_Ψ]_k − Σ_k [u_{N0}]_k), and rerun or qualify the numerical claim.
issues.overall_effect: The stated structure-preserving (conservation) feature of the trained reduced model in Test 3 is not delivered by the algorithm as written.
issues.title: Conservation loss term is identical to the reconstruction loss and does not enforce conservation of total concentration
issues.why_classification: A local change of the loss term repairs the construction; no theoretical result depends on it.
